doc.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007

title: Cannonball Adderley and Nancy Wilson live
summary: He saw Nancy Wilson with Cannonball in Cleveland at 18 and explains why Cannonball influenced him, including the Latin influence of Feldman's Azule Serape.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: I love the record too. She’s got these cool arrangements with Cannonball and Nat.

Oh yeah. I saw them live in Cleveland when I was 18 years old and there was a great club called Leo’s Casino, and you had to put leis around your neck because you couldn’t drink at 18, and you had these Hawaiian leis on your neck and my future wife and I were sitting there, and we saw Cannonball and Nancy and loved every minute of it.
Oh you saw the two of them together.
Oh it was sizzling. I loved it.
Me too. I quote him in a lyric, Cannonball.
I do, in “Keeper of the Flame.”
What was it that grabbed you about him?
Well you know everybody loves Charlie Parker you know. And I love Charlie too, but I think Cannonball did more with less. He swung harder with less. Do you feel that way?
I think, plus his tone was, I mean as a saxophone player it’s like well there you go.

There you go. And he used the Latin thing and he expanded, he was a big influence as far as my Latin thing, you know. There was a great tune by Victor Feldman, “Azule Serape.” Oh, what a great tune, knocked me down, loved it.
